# Relationship between the two jump sequences

The video contains one physical jump shown twice. The second jump sequence is a half-speed slow-motion replay of the first, not a second, different jump.

Points stated explicitly:

1. There is a hard cut at about 2.43 s, between frame 73 and frame 74 of 219 at 30 fps. Frames 1–73 are the first sequence, about 2.43 s. Frames 74–219 are the second sequence, about 4.87 s, exactly twice as long: 73 frames versus 146 frames.

2. Both sequences follow the same rink path in the same direction with the same camera pan. The skater starts in front of the saatva.com/AARP/gusto boards skating toward the left of the rink, takes off in front of the CDW/saatva.com boards, is airborne past the OLLIE'S/CDW boards, lands, and glides out past the OLLIE'S/CDW and GIVE TODAY boards. The background advertisement sequence AARP to CDW to OLLIE'S repeats in the same order and orientation.

3. Frame-by-frame comparison with a 2:1 mapping matches. Frame N in the first sequence matches frame 74 + 2×(N−1) in the second sequence. Examples: frame 10 matches frame 92, frame 20 matches frame 112, frame 30 matches frame 132, frame 40 matches frame 152, frame 50 matches frame 172, frame 60 matches frame 192, frame 70 matches frame 212. In each pair the skater's pose, arm and leg positions, rotational phase, position relative to the boards, the standing observer at the boards, the crowd, stairs, seats, and flags are the same.

4. It is the same skater in the same costume doing the same element. Takeoff posture, in-air tuck with arms crossed, rotation direction, and landing posture on one foot gliding backward with arms opening are identical at matched phases.

5. The second sequence is not mirrored, not reversed, and not a different attempt. Board text reads correctly in both, motion direction is the same leftward travel, and rotation proceeds the same way. A reversed copy would swap takeoff and landing; a mirror copy would reverse text; a different attempt would differ in body positions, ice marks, crowd clapping phase, and observer posture. None of those differences occur.

6. The slow motion is smooth interpolated half speed, not frozen frames. Consecutive frames within the second sequence, for example 91-92-93 or 151-152-153, show continuous intermediate positions of the skater and background, so each original frame interval is expanded into about two frames.

Therefore the two sequences have the same takeoff, same number of rotations, same landing, and same outcome. Anything judged about the jump from the first sequence applies equally to the second; the second only makes the same action easier to inspect because it lasts twice as long.
